PAPERS.short: Guangdong CHD PM2.5 constituents 2026
PAPERS.title: Differential Impacts of Fine Particulate Matter Constituents on Congenital Heart Disease across Critical Periconceptional Windows
PAPERS.pm: Residential PM2.5 mass and constituents (sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, BC, OM) by periconceptional window
PAPERS.n: Guangdong CHD Registry 2004-2022: 12,680 cases, 10,266 controls, multilevel logistic regression by exposure window. Per-IQR increments of PM2.5 mass and constituents raised CHD odds 9-16%, strongest in the preconception window and attenuating later; BC and nitrate stayed associated during pregnancy. Conotruncal defects carried the largest ORs (1.14-1.36 per IQR). Mixture models put sulfate and BC first preconception, BC and nitrate thereafter. Limitation: constituents are modelled and mutually collinear, so 'dominant constituent' rankings are mixture-model artefacts as much as biology; registry controls and the higher-SES amplification hint at ascertainment differences. CIs absent from the abstract. Relevance: moderate - constituent-resolved windows need speciation, which optical LCS cannot supply; BC from multi-wavelength nodes is the tractable piece.

PAPERS.short: UKB arrhythmia NMR metabolome mediation 2026
PAPERS.title: Large-scale plasma metabolic profiling identifies signatures and biomarkers associated with air pollution and arrhythmias: A prospective cohort study from UK Biobank
PAPERS.pm: LUR PM2.5, PM10, NO2, NOx at baseline residence
PAPERS.n: 449,068 UK Biobank participants free of arrhythmia, median follow-up 16.3 y, 47,381 incident cases. All four pollutants were associated with arrhythmia, HR 1.015-1.257 per 10 ug/m3 (range across pollutants; CIs not in the abstract). An elastic-net signature from 170 NMR metabolites mediated 11.2% of the PM2.5 association (PM10 5.2%, NO2 7.4%, NOx 9.8%); lipid, ketone-body and amino-acid pathways recurred, ketone bodies most for intraventricular block. Limitation: single-baseline 2010 LUR exposure and single-time metabolomics make mediation cross-sectional in disguise; ketone bodies track fasting and diabetes status. Relevance: low-moderate for sensing - another UKB LUR result whose exposure contrast is too smooth to need dense monitoring.

PAPERS.short: Creosote railroad switch PAH workers 2026
PAPERS.title: Assessing PAH exposure during construction work of railroad switches using creosote-impregnated ties
PAPERS.pm: Full-shift breathing-zone PAH (16 EPA priority; particle + vapour), dermal tape strips, urinary 1-HP
PAPERS.n: Workers assembling railroad switches from creosote ties: breathing-zone sum of 16 PAHs 120,000-280,000 ng/m3 on a single sampled shift; skin pyrene 0.31-140 ng/cm2, highest on palms and calves; urinary 1-HP rose across the week (1.9-17 umol/mol creatinine), most above the UK guidance value by day 4. A PBTK model attributed uptake mainly to the dermal route, and pyrene under protective clothing implies fabric penetration. Limitation: one air-sampling shift, small crew, and the particle/vapour split is not reported, so the inhalation share rests on the model. Relevance: low for ambient sensing - a reminder that biomarker-based particulate PAH exposure is not reducible to air concentration.

PAPERS.short: Pu Lima hybrid transfer-learning PM2.5 2026
PAPERS.title: A Hybrid Transfer Learning Approach for Ambient PM2.5 Exposure Modeling in LMIC Contexts: A Case Study from Lima, Peru
PAPERS.pm: Daily 1 km PM2.5 from reference + low-cost monitors, MAIAC AOD, WRF-Chem and covariates
PAPERS.n: Lima 2010-2023 daily PM2.5 surface from an instance-weighted random forest that fuses reference and low-cost monitor data, satellite AOD and WRF-Chem. Sampling bias toward monitored districts is handled by geo-environmental similarity transfer learning that borrows weighted training instances from the US. Cross-validated R2 0.76; predicted mean PM2.5 in mountainous districts fell from 34.19 to 29.23 ug/m3 versus the unweighted model. Limitation: CV R2 is computed on the same biased monitor locations the method claims to correct, so the mountain-region gain is unverified by held-out sites there; how low-cost data were calibrated is not stated. Relevance: high - a template for using sparse LCS networks plus transfer learning in data-poor cities.

PAPERS.short: SEARO air-quality early-warning review 2026
PAPERS.title: Prediction accuracy of available early warning systems for air pollution across WHO South-East Asia region: a systematic review
PAPERS.pm: Forecast PM2.5 and other pollutants (RMSE, R2, categorical accuracy, bias)
PAPERS.n: PROSPERO-registered review (to Feb 2026): 14 modelling studies from 839 records, PROBAST+AI risk-of-bias. Hybrid deep-learning forecasters reported the lowest RMSE (0.84-4.61 ug/m3) and R2 up to 0.998 for PM2.5; ML reached 98.3% categorical accuracy; CTMs cut bias ~70% only with satellite data assimilation. Most studies were at high risk of bias from absent external validation and overfitting; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Limitation: an R2 of 0.998 for daily PM2.5 is a leakage signature, and the review reports such figures without re-analysis. Relevance: moderate - operational forecast skill in the region is unproven; LCS networks could provide the out-of-sample validation these systems lack.

PAPERS.short: Gujral Dominici Memphis datacenter PM2.5 2026
PAPERS.title: Behind-the-Meter Versus Grid Electricity for AI Datacenters: Magnitude, Geography, and Equity of PM2.5-Attributable Mortality in Memphis
PAPERS.pm: Modelled population-weighted PM2.5 from on-site turbines vs grid generation
PAPERS.n: Two datacenters 12 km apart. At a common 240 MW, grid-supplied C1 carried 10.83 attributable deaths/y (95% interval 7.83-13.84) vs 3.67 (2.65-4.68) for behind-the-meter C2; at real/permitted capacities the order reversed, 11.35 (6.48-17.29) for C2 vs 8.10 (4.60-12.38) for C1. 94% of C1 deaths fell >250 km away; 82% of C2 deaths within 50 km, concentrated in the low-income, high people-of-colour stratum. Limitation: preprint; permitted capacity is not operating capacity, and on-site turbine emission factors and the reduced-form dispersion model are the whole result. Relevance: high - a near-source burden that a local LCS network around the site could verify directly.

PAPERS.short: Yoon pollutant asthma immune mechanisms review 2026
PAPERS.title: Impacts and Immune Mechanisms of Pollutant-Mediated Asthma and Airway Inflammation
PAPERS.pm: PM, DEP, O3, NO2, SO2, VOCs, bioaerosols
PAPERS.n: Narrative review of epithelial injury, barrier disruption, oxidative stress and innate signalling (NF-kB, MAPK, PI3K/Akt, inflammasome) driving T2, non-T2 and mixed asthma phenotypes; pollutant-specific arms include PM-induced NLRP3 activation, O3 barrier disruption, DEP-driven IL-17A and pollutant-allergen co-exposure. Acknowledges that experimental doses and compositions do not map onto real-world exposure. Limitation: non-systematic, no new data, and no dose metric that a measurement study could target. Relevance: low - background for mechanism sections.

PAPERS.short: GBD 2023 G20 stroke air pollution temperature 2026
PAPERS.title: Estimates, temporal evolution, and contributors of the stroke burden due to air pollution and non-optimal temperature across G20 nations, 1990-2023
PAPERS.pm: GBD ambient PM and household solid-fuel pollution; non-optimal temperature
PAPERS.n: GBD 2023, G20 nations. Age-standardised stroke mortality attributable to air pollution plus non-optimal temperature fell from 52.81 to 17.46/100,000 (1990-2023; EAPC -3.44%, 95% CI -3.57 to -3.30); DALY rate EAPC -3.29%. The decline is driven by household air pollution; ambient PM and heat burdens rose or stalled, highest in low/middle-SDI members, and ARIMA projections to 2040 keep them flat. Limitation: GBD re-tabulation with joint attribution of two risk classes; the ARIMA projection adds no exposure information. Relevance: low - confirms that ambient PM, not household fuel, now carries the residual stroke burden.

PAPERS.short: MESA long-term air pollution suPAR null 2026
PAPERS.title: Long-term ambient air pollution is not associated with circulating soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor
PAPERS.pm: MESA Air spatiotemporal PM2.5, NO2, NOx, O3, light-absorbing carbon (long-term residential)
PAPERS.n: 5,072 MESA participants (2000-2002 enrolment), ELISA suPAR, multivariable linear regression. No pollutant - PM2.5, NO2, NOx, O3 or light-absorbing carbon - was associated with suPAR; the PM2.5 CI excluded effects of 2% or more per 5 ug/m3. With two prior null cohorts, the authors conclude suPAR is not a meaningful mediator of the PM-CVD link. Limitation: single cross-sectional suPAR measure, and the US contrast of the early 2000s is narrow relative to high-exposure settings, so a null at 5 ug/m3 does not transfer to them. Relevance: low-moderate - a well-powered null worth citing against biomarker-mediation claims; the exposure model, not sensors, sets the contrast.

PAPERS.short: Atlante Aria e Salute Delphi co-creation 2026
PAPERS.title: Co-creation as a decision-making tool in the PNC 'Atlante Aria e Salute' project to define the contents of an integrated atlas
PAPERS.pm: Outdoor PM2.5, PM10, NO2, O3 (atlas exposure layers)
PAPERS.n: Two Delphi rounds (16 then 22 experts and regional stakeholders) plus plenaries to fix the Italian national air-and-health atlas: data sources (ISTAT cause-specific mortality, hospital discharges), territorial disaggregation, pollutant-outcome pairs graded on causal certainty, public-health relevance and routine-data accuracy, attributable-fraction methods and policy counterfactuals. Limitation: process paper; the abstract is truncated before the final outcome list, and no exposure model is specified. Relevance: low-moderate - a national open-data atlas is a natural consumer of fused monitor/LCS exposure surfaces if its resolution is fine enough.

PAPERS.short: Air-health web atlases review Italy 2026
PAPERS.title: PNC project 'Atlante Aria e Salute': exploratory web review and quality assessment of open-access atlases on the health effects of air pollution
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5/PM10 (all platforms), NO2 and O3 (fewer)
PAPERS.n: Protocol-driven review of public air-and-health atlases (Sep-Dec 2024): 1,000 websites screened, 15 potentially relevant, 8 included (3 governmental, 3 academic, 2 foundations). All report PM2.5 and/or PM10; NO2 and O3 are less common; all but one use annual averages, six give dose-response estimates (mostly all-cause long-term mortality), only two cause-specific. Assessed for interactivity, Flesch readability, WCAG accessibility and transparency. Limitation: eight sites is a thin sample and search-engine screening is not reproducible. Relevance: moderate - public health-impact maps ignore sub-annual and sub-city variation, exactly what dense networks measure.

PAPERS.short: Torii Kalimantan peat fire super-linear scaling 2026
PAPERS.title: Peat Burning Scales Super-linearly with Fire-Season Magnitude in the West Kalimantan-Sarawak Border Region, 2012-2025
PAPERS.pm: VIIRS active-fire detections on peat vs non-peat; FRP; back-trajectories to Sarawak receptors
PAPERS.n: Fourteen fire seasons of VIIRS detections against a peat map: peat-fire counts scale with total detections as a power law, exponent 1.96 (95% CI 1.57-2.36; R2 0.89), so doubling fire activity quadruples peat burning; robust to alternative predictors (2.36) and a Suomi-NPP-only subset (1.98). Peat share rises from <4% in La Nina years to 30-51% in El Nino years (ONI r 0.78), though ONI is collinear with season size. 24.3% of cells burning >=7 years gave 57.7% of cumulative FRP; scaling survives back-trajectory transport (1.59). Limitation: single-author preprint, detections not emissions, and no PM observations close the chain. Relevance: moderate - receptor-site sensors in Sarawak could test whether haze PM really tracks the squared term.

PAPERS.short: Lung-on-a-chip pollutant toxicity review 2026
PAPERS.title: Microfluidic lung-on-a-chip for evaluating inflammation and toxicity from environmental pollutants
PAPERS.pm: Atmospheric PM, pathogens, VOCs, aromatic hydrocarbons, micro/nanomaterials (in vitro)
PAPERS.endpoint: Inflammation and toxicity in lung-on-a-chip models
PAPERS.n: Review of microfluidic lung-on-a-chip platforms - air-liquid interface, cyclic stretch, perfused endothelium - for pollutant toxicology, covering PM, pathogens, VOCs and emerging nanomaterials, with advantages in biomimicry and real-time readout and the obstacles of chip standardisation, operational complexity and subsystem integration. Limitation: no quantitative synthesis; dose delivery (deposited mass per area) is the variable that decides translatability and is not addressed in the abstract. Relevance: low - only connects to monitoring if chips are dosed at measured ambient deposition rates.

PAPERS.short: Guangdong COPD surveillance PM1 PM2.5 PM10 PAF 2026
PAPERS.title: Association between chronic respiratory diseases and the attributable risk of long-term exposure to atmospheric particulate matters among middle-aged and elderly Chinese population
PAPERS.pm: 722-day mean PM1, PM2.5, PM10 at 1 km (residential address, 2013-2019)
PAPERS.endpoint: Chronic respiratory disease, COPD, chronic bronchitis, asthma
PAPERS.n: COPD surveillance sample of 7,371 adults >=40 y (CRD 19.4%, COPD 10.0%). Each 10 ug/m3 of PM was associated with higher prevalence of every CRD outcome, more so in rural residents and biomass users. PAF of CRD: PM1 19.09% (95% CI 12.41-25.02), PM2.5 18.98% (12.90-24.90), PM10 21.40% (13.84-27.67); COPD highest. Limitation: cross-sectional prevalence, so PAF here is causal only by assumption; PM1/PM2.5/PM10 come from the same satellite-ML product and are near-collinear, so the three PAFs are one estimate three times; biomass fuel confounds rural contrasts. Relevance: low-moderate - PM1 adds nothing distinct when derived from the same model.

PAPERS.short: Schafer AERONET lunar AOD assessment 2026
PAPERS.title: An assessment of lunar photometry in AERONET
PAPERS.pm: Night-time lunar AOD (440-1640 nm), Angstrom exponent, SDA fine/coarse AOD
PAPERS.n: CIMEL model-T lunar AOD at 492 sites since 2014 with an updated empirical correction to the ROLO lunar irradiance model. At all long-record sites, day-night AOD differences are typically within +/-0.01 at 440 nm and as good or better at longer wavelengths; in 3 h day/night transition windows under low, stable AOD, AOD, Angstrom exponent, water vapour and SDA fine/coarse AOD show statistically negligible differences. Limitation: agreement is shown only under stable low AOD - smoke and dust nights, where night AOD matters most, are untested, and lunar-phase coverage leaves gaps. Relevance: high - validated night-time AOD removes the daytime-only constraint on AOD-PM2.5 fusion and gives LCS networks a night-time column reference.

PAPERS.short: Monsoon aerosol Pb isotopes rainwater offsets 2026
PAPERS.title: Monsoon-related variability of water-soluble aerosol Pb isotopes and systematic aerosol-rainwater offsets at Peng Chia Yu
PAPERS.pm: Water-soluble aerosol Pb isotopes vs rainwater
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates monsoon-resolved variation in water-soluble aerosol Pb isotope ratios and systematic offsets between aerosol and rainwater signatures. Recorded for coverage; no estimate inferred. Relevance: low - source apportionment input, not a monitoring method.

PAPERS.short: Multi-scale PM2.5 nonlinear time-series two metros 2026
PAPERS.title: Deciphering multi-scale PM2.5 temporal dynamics and cross-scale interactions in two climatically distinct metropolitan areas: insights from advanced nonlinear time-series analysis
PAPERS.pm: Monitor PM2.5 time series (multi-scale decomposition)
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates nonlinear multi-scale decomposition of PM2.5 series and cross-scale interactions in two climatically distinct metropolitan areas (author affiliations suggest Vietnam/Taiwan). Recorded for coverage; no estimate inferred. Relevance: low-moderate - scale separation is how network redundancy and siting density are usually argued.

PAPERS.short: Bachour WRF-Chem AOD post-correction hot desert 2026
PAPERS.title: Statistical post-correction of WRF-Chem aerosol optical depth under hot-desert conditions
PAPERS.pm: WRF-Chem AOD vs ground photometry
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates statistical bias correction of WRF-Chem AOD in a hot-desert setting (author group based in Qatar). Recorded for coverage; no estimate inferred. Relevance: moderate - dust-dominated AOD is where both models and optical LCS fail, and corrected CTM fields are common fusion inputs.

PAPERS.short: Zhou condensation sink efficiency hygroscopicity 2026
PAPERS.title: Condensation Sink Efficiency of Atmospheric Particles Regulated by Their Chemical Compositions and Hygroscopicity
PAPERS.pm: Pre-existing particle condensation sink toward H2SO4/HIO3; composition and hygroscopicity
PAPERS.n: Defines a CS efficiency coefficient (epsilon = CS_eff/CS_calc, the latter assuming irreversible uptake) for gaseous H2SO4. Epsilon depends on composition and water uptake: dry pure organics scavenge less efficiently than inorganics, high RH raises epsilon for both, and mixed particles sit between, set jointly by composition and RH; CS efficiency is lower still for HIO3. Including epsilon improves cluster-survival and sub-3 nm formation simulations and may explain intense NPF despite high CS in megacities. Limitation: epsilon values and their uncertainty are not given in the abstract, and field transfer is 'exploratory'. Relevance: low-moderate - NPF bursts drive number, not mass, so optical LCS miss them; CPC-equipped nodes would not.

PAPERS.short: Harbin ammonium PM2.5 and precipitation sources 2026
PAPERS.title: From atmosphere to river: Tracing the origins and deposition of ammonium in both PM2.5 and precipitation in Harbin
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 ammonium (isotopic source tracing) and wet deposition
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates source tracing of ammonium in PM2.5 and precipitation in Harbin and its deposition to river systems. Recorded for coverage; no estimate inferred. Relevance: low - secondary inorganic aerosol source apportionment.

PAPERS.short: Shandong integrated air-pollutant GHG inventory 2026
PAPERS.title: Strategies for Co-Control of Air Pollutants and Greenhouse Gases: Insights from an Integrated Emission Inventory in Shandong Province
PAPERS.pm: Primary PM, SO2, NOx, VOCs, NH3, CO plus CO2, CH4, N2O by source and city
PAPERS.n: 2024 integrated inventory for 16 Shandong prefectures, 10 air pollutants and 4 GHGs over 8 source categories. Power/heat and industry gave 86.84% of CO2; industry dominated SO2, CO and VOCs; mobile sources NOx; agriculture NH3, CH4 and N2O; fugitive dust dominated primary PM. Interspecies correlations show partial synergy, so co-control cannot be assumed from shared sources. Limitation: inventory only, no uncertainty bounds in the abstract, and fugitive-dust PM is the least constrained category in any inventory. Relevance: low-moderate - fugitive dust dominance is a coarse-mode signal that PM10/PM2.5 ratios from LCS can check locally.

PAPERS.short: Epple DLR tire-wear particle chassis dynamometer 2026
PAPERS.title: Temperature and Inflation Pressure Effects on Airborne Tire Wear Particle Measurements on a Chassis Dynamometer
PAPERS.pm: Airborne TRWP number (MCPC 7 nm-2 um; OPS 0.3-10 um) and OPS mass proxy
PAPERS.n: Two-level factorial (inflation 1.8/3.8 bar x chamber 11/35 C) on the DLR TRWP system, in two blocks of toe setting. Higher temperature raised cumulative MCPC response 3.6-fold (95% CI 1.8-7.2); higher pressure cut OPS number 18% (12-24%); OPS mass proxy fell ~17% with temperature. Toe >48 arcmin produced rising signals and irregular wear. Reference-condition MCPC response doubled over the campaign, so drift monitoring and randomised blocked run order are prerequisites. Limitation: one tire, one rig; the OPS mass proxy assumes density and refractive index; the ultrafine mode may be volatile, not wear. Relevance: moderate - non-exhaust PM metrology with explicit instrument drift; the same discipline applies to LCS.

PAPERS.short: Cheng BTH multi-source satellite PM2.5 stacking 2026
PAPERS.title: Machine Learning-Based Retrieval of PM2.5 Concentrations Using Multi-Source Satellite Data in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Region of China
PAPERS.pm: Satellite AOD + LST, NDVI, tropospheric NO2 + meteorology -> surface PM2.5
PAPERS.n: BTH 2019-2021: RF, SVR, XGBoost and linear stacking on four predictor sets with an 80:10:10 split. Test R2 rose from 0.51-0.54 with AOD alone to 0.83-0.84 with all eight predictors; stacking best at R2 0.84, RMSE 12.4, MAE 9.7 ug/m3. Southern/southwestern Hebei highest; winter > summer. Missing AOD limited spatial completeness. Limitation: a random split leaks spatial and temporal autocorrelation, so the test R2 overstates out-of-site skill; no spatial-block CV, and gap filling - the real problem - is left to future work. Relevance: moderate - AOD alone explains half the variance; ground nodes and meteorology carry the rest.

PAPERS.short: Walter neighbourhood air exchange inhaled dose children 2026
PAPERS.title: Neighborhood-scale disparities in air exchange rates and inhaled pollution dose among school-aged children
PAPERS.pm: Residential air exchange rate and infiltrated PM / inhaled dose
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates neighbourhood-scale modelling of housing air exchange rates and the resulting inhaled pollutant dose among school-aged children, framed as a disparity analysis (Northeastern University group). Recorded for coverage; no estimate inferred. Relevance: high if infiltration is parameterised from data - indoor/outdoor LCS pairs measure exactly this ratio.

PAPERS.short: UKB women deprivation PM2.5-NO2 fatty liver 2026
PAPERS.title: Socioeconomic disadvantage, air pollution, and metabolic health among women: analyses of UK Biobank and US data
PAPERS.pm: 2010 residential PM2.5-NO2 score (UK); state PM2.5 (US)
PAPERS.endpoint: Fatty Liver Index, MRI liver fat, obesity prevalence
PAPERS.n: 231,525 UK Biobank women: Townsend deprivation predicted FLI (beta 1.114, 95% CI 1.069-1.159) and FLI>=60 (OR 1.080, 1.076-1.084). Age-adjusted pollution associations vanished once deprivation entered the model (FLI beta -0.068, -0.137 to 0.001; FLI>=60 OR 0.999, 0.993-1.004). Across 46 US jurisdictions, +1 SD poverty meant +1.38 points female obesity after PM2.5 adjustment. Limitation: adjusting for an area deprivation index that partly lies on the pollution pathway can over-adjust; a 2010 LUR score and state-level US PM2.5 are coarse. The null is contextual, not causal. Relevance: low-moderate - shows how easily SES absorbs smooth LUR contrasts; finer exposure would be needed to separate them.
